Definition: {properly, to wander away, i.e. lose oneself; by implication to perish (causative, destroy)}
BiblicalUsage: This is the ordinary word for perishing in both Hebrew and Aramaic — to wander away and be lost, and so to be destroyed. The psalm says ‘the way of the ungodly shall perish’; Moses warns Israel that if they forget the LORD ‘ye shall surely perish’; and Daniel prays in Aramaic that he and his friends ‘should not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon’.
TheologicalSignificance: Perishing in the Bible is not an accident; it is the end of a road walked away from God. I believe the warning is also a kindness — Moses tells Israel plainly what will happen if they forget, because God would rather warn than destroy — and Daniel’s prayer shows the other side: the God who judges is the God who spares when His people pray.
